definition.name: web_search
definition.description: Search the public web for current or external information. Use this for recent information, public sources, and research that needs citations; Butler may plan multiple focused searches internally when smart search planning is enabled. For broad research, discover sources without a domain filter first; if a filtered or source-specific search is empty or blocked, broaden the query or use another accessible authoritative or reputable source.

query.description: Search request or missing evidence. For broad research, let Butler plan diverse sources instead of narrowing every search to a few sites.

allowed_domains.description: Strict result filter for every planned search. Omit it for broad or multi-source research because it can exclude useful alternative evidence. Use it when the user requires specific domains or for a deliberately narrow follow-up on known sources.

blocked_domains.description: Exclude results from these domains while leaving other sources available.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return.

definition.name: web_read
definition.description: Read a public URL through Butler's configured page-reader stack and return bounded page evidence. Use after web_search when snippets are insufficient for exact quotes, current news, or source-backed claims. When content_has_more is true, continue with start_chunk set to next_start_chunk; returned_chunks counts only complete chunks included in the current result. If a page is unavailable, search for an accessible source covering the same requested fact.

max_chars.description: Maximum markdown characters returned for the selected chunk window (1500-8000, default 2000). The minimum fits one built-in evidence chunk. Use start_chunk, not a larger max_chars, to continue reading later chunks.

max_chunks.description: Maximum evidence chunks returned from start_chunk (1-8, default 1).

start_chunk.description: Zero-based chunk offset for continuing through the page (default 0). Use next_start_chunk from the previous result.

definition.name: transform_public_data_table
definition.description: Create a bounded CSV artifact and preview from a small set of public, non-secret row objects.

title.description: Short public label for the transformed table.

columns.description: Column names to keep in the CSV, in output order.

rows.description: Public row objects with primitive values only.

definition.name: run_command
definition.description: Run a non-interactive command in the active workspace through Butler's platform-neutral command executor. summary is the compact model-authored action label shown to the user, such as '실행: git commit', '커밋 후 푸시', or '검증: bun test'; it never authorizes execution. Set validation_suite for validation receipts. Put generated artifacts under $BUTLER_ARTIFACTS_DIR, and list intentional existing workspace deliverables in output_paths. Prefer cross-platform executables and JSON-safe command text.

command.description: Non-interactive command; prefer cross-platform executables, explicit arguments, and focused output.

summary.description: Required one-line model-authored action label based on the actual command, at most 32 characters. Use compact labels such as '실행: git commit', '커밋 후 푸시', or '검증: bun test'; do not write a purpose sentence or include arguments, paths, messages, URLs, or secrets. Presentation only; it cannot authorize or alter the command or result.

cwd.description: Optional contained workspace directory; relative paths use its root.

max_output_tokens.description: Optional preview token budget, default 1200, applied range 200-8000. The result reports requested/applied limits and truncation. Omitted output stays in the existing artifact reader.

output_paths.description: Existing regular files to publish as deliverables after success, not directories or globs. Omit for ordinary source changes and build directories; file changes are tracked separately. Use artifacts/generated/... for $BUTLER_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Publication failure is separate from command exit status and success.

validation_suite.description: Stable validation suite id used only for validation evidence and output presentation. It never selects a sandbox or execution environment.

state_effect.description: Effect intent: mutation and remote_observation require accepted Plan Review and admitted execution authority; ask_first suspends for approval and resumes after approval, while full_access uses existing authority. For read_only and validation, the admitted access mode owns the execution environment; validation_suite only labels evidence.

output_mode.description: Preview only: auto suppresses successes with validation_suite and bounds failures; silent_on_success suppresses successes; full avoids suppression and failure-tail reduction but still obeys the preview token cap. Original stdout/stderr remains retrievable for every omitted portion.

definition.name: read_file
definition.description: Read 1-20 bounded UTF-8 workspace files in request order with path guard, binary/UTF-8 checks, aggregate limits, stale-safe continuation, and evidence receipts. Use a one-item requests array for one file.

requests.description: Canonical bounded read requests. Use one item for one file.

path.description: File path inside the active workspace. Prefer a workspace-relative path; a contained absolute path shown by a tool is also accepted.

limit_lines.description: Total requested line range, including cursor continuations. Later file lines are outside this request.

definition.name: read_project_source
definition.description: Read the complete, immutable public project source snapshot explicitly attached to this turn. Use originalRef.fileId from project source context. Continue with next_cursor until truncated is false. This reads the accepted snapshot, not current live Ledger state; arbitrary paths and other files are not accepted.

file_id.description: Exact originalRef.fileId from the attached project source context.

cursor.description: First page: omit or use an empty string. Later pages: copy next_cursor exactly from the previous result. Never invent a cursor.

definition.name: write_file
definition.description: Set one UTF-8 workspace file to its complete desired content. The runtime safely creates a missing file or replaces an existing file after observing its current bytes. content is never a patch, fragment, or append; use edit_file for a small exact change to an existing file. Use Project Ledger tools for Ledger files.

path.description: Workspace-relative path; not an absolute path or workspace root.

definition.name: edit_file
definition.description: Apply one exact text edit or an ordered batch of exact text edits to existing workspace files. Repeated paths are allowed: later edits address the preceding in-memory result, and each file is committed once. The runtime observes each file and injects its stale-state guard; provide only path, start_line, old_text, and new_text. Use Project Ledger tools for Ledger files.

path.description: File path inside the active workspace. Prefer a workspace-relative path; a contained absolute path shown by a tool is also accepted.

start_line.description: Optional one-based location hint for old_text. It may be stale after earlier edits; the exact text remains authoritative.

old_text.description: Exact existing text copied from the current file. Include indentation and line breaks exactly as they appear.

new_text.description: Exact replacement text. An empty string removes old_text.

edits.description: Ordered exact edits, including repeated paths. Later edits address preceding results. Runtime guards each file's initial state and commits it once.

definition.name: grep_files
definition.description: Search UTF-8 workspace text with a regular expression (literal=false), or exact text (literal=true). Use root and include_globs/exclude_globs to narrow discovery; continue with the returned next_cursor when present. Runtime owns traversal and output budgets.

pattern.description: Pattern searched inside the active workspace; paths and globs are workspace-relative.

root.description: Workspace-relative directory to search. Defaults to the active workspace root.

literal.description: Use false for regular expressions such as foo|bar; true to match the pattern as exact text.

definition.name: list_files
definition.description: Discover regular files under a guarded workspace directory with deterministic bounded results. Use root and include_globs/exclude_globs to narrow discovery, then read a candidate with read_file.

root.description: Workspace-relative directory to inspect. Defaults to the active workspace root.

include_globs.description: Optional workspace-relative file globs applied during traversal.

exclude_globs.description: Optional workspace-relative file or directory globs excluded during traversal.

definition.name: bind_session_git_worktree
definition.description: Create or select a safe linked Git worktree and bind it as this project session's canonical workspace. The target path is derived by Butler; no path or destructive Git operation is accepted.

action.description: create a linked branch worktree or select an already linked branch worktree.

branch.description: Git branch short name; refs, revisions, control characters, and leading dashes are rejected.

start_point.description: Optional Git commit/ref used only as create's branch start point.

definition.name: project_ledger_index
definition.description: Rebuild the compact Ledger index.

definition.name: project_ledger_status
definition.description: Read Ledger summary, staleness, and next actions.

definition.name: project_ledger_list
definition.description: List bounded Ledger records by kind, status, or query. Omitted or blank kind lists all kinds.

kind.description: Query kind; all (default) includes every record kind. Omitted or blank means all.

definition.name: project_ledger_show
definition.description: Read one Ledger record, optionally with its body.

definition.name: project_ledger_create
definition.description: Create one Ledger record. Search with project_ledger_list first. task needs work_id; attempt needs task_id; work/task needs acceptance.

definition.name: project_ledger_update
definition.description: Update one exact Ledger record by kind and id.

definition.name: project_ledger_work_update
definition.description: Update or transition one Work.

definition.name: project_ledger_work_complete
definition.description: Complete Work with validation, review, and report. For required Git evidence, use code_commit:"auto"; code_commits accepts canonical JSON. Missing Git is recoverable and does not block Butler.

code_commit.description: Use "auto" for active workspace HEAD; never pass a SHA.

definition.name: project_ledger_task_update
definition.description: Update or transition one Task.

definition.name: project_ledger_task_complete
definition.description: Complete a Task with validation, review, and report evidence.

code_commit.description: Use "auto" for active workspace HEAD; never pass a SHA.

definition.name: project_ledger_attempt_start
definition.description: Start an Attempt under a Task.

definition.name: project_ledger_attempt_succeed
definition.description: Mark an Attempt succeeded.

definition.name: project_ledger_attempt_fail
definition.description: Mark an Attempt failed.

definition.name: project_ledger_render
definition.description: Render a Ledger view; persist only when write is true.

definition.name: project_ledger_check
definition.description: Validate Ledger records and return safe issues.

definition.name: get_work_dashboard
definition.description: Read Butler's canonical work dashboard: active work, recoverable work, failures, report-ready items, and delivery backlog.

debug.description: When true, include raw task and delivery identifiers for operator troubleshooting.

definition.name: inspect_project_status
definition.description: Inspect active Project Ledger status without broad file reads.

project_ref.description: Project id/name/workspace/canonical root; omit for active project.

definition.name: query_project_work
definition.description: Query active Project Ledger next actions, blockers, specs, risks, or stale views.

project_ref.description: Project id/name/workspace/canonical root; omit for active project.

definition.name: render_project_dashboard
definition.description: Render active Project Ledger dashboard, handoff, or roadmap views.

project_ref.description: Project id/name/workspace/canonical root; omit for active project.

write.description: When true, write the generated view under the active Project Ledger views directory.

definition.name: complete_project_work
definition.description: Complete a Project Ledger work item through the same evidence gate used by the CLI.

project_ref.description: Project id/name/workspace/canonical root; omit for active project.

definition.name: get_context_monitor
definition.description: Inspect safe context pressure telemetry for the active session: prompt sizes, recall size, transcript growth, and estimated token pressure without raw prompt text.

session_id.description: Optional session id. Defaults to the active Butler session when available.

definition.name: read_operation_results
definition.description: Read an exact stored result or its original request (source=request). Find references with list_operation_results. Decode data from base64; continue at nextOffset until null. The last page may be shorter.

definition.name: list_operation_results
definition.description: Find prior tool requests/results in this Turn and its existing Work without repeating the operation. Start with cursor=0 and through=null. Search a literal substring of request text (not separate keywords); leave query empty to filter only by tool/status. Use returned exact_read with read_operation_results. Continue with next_cursor and the returned through watermark; request previews may be shortened, originals remain readable.

status.description: Operation outcome: completed means success, failed includes returned tool errors, nonzero exit codes and timeouts; cancelled means cancelled execution. null searches all outcomes.

through.description: null for the first page; thereafter copy through from the previous page.

definition.name: read_tool_evidence_artifact
definition.description: Read original saved tool evidence. Continue exactly by passing next_offset_chars as offset_chars; whitespace and line endings are preserved.

offset_lines.description: Zero-based starting line; ignored when offset_chars is supplied.

offset_chars.description: Exact UTF-16 character offset from next_offset_chars, including within a long line.

definition.name: read_tool_output_artifact
definition.description: Read or search the original saved stdout/stderr without rerunning the command. For exact continuation select one stream and pass its next_offset_chars as offset_chars, omitting search. Text preserves whitespace and line endings; offsets count UTF-16 characters.

offset_lines.description: Zero-based starting line; ignored when offset_chars is supplied.

offset_chars.description: Exact zero-based UTF-16 character offset, including within a long line. Use the selected stream's next_offset_chars for lossless continuation.

search.description: Case-sensitive literal substring. Return a slice beginning at the first match at or after the offset; search metadata reports no match explicitly.

limit_lines.description: Line budget, default 80, applied range 1-500; actual limits are returned.

max_tokens.description: Combined estimated text-token budget, default 1200, applied range 50-8000; actual and per-stream budgets are returned.

definition.name: get_usage_monitor
definition.description: Inspect safe model/cache, web-search, and tool usage counters without raw prompts, messages, tool arguments, or tool results.

session_id.description: Optional session id for transcript-derived tool usage.

since_hours.description: Optional lookback window in hours for timestamped metrics.

definition.name: list_tool_capabilities
definition.description: List Butler's available and disabled native tools with categories, safety notes, and disabled reasons.

category.description: Optional category filter. command=shell, file=filesystem; all/native/workspace mean no filter.

include_disabled.description: Whether to include disabled tools. Defaults to true.

definition.name: tool_search
definition.description: Search Butler's compact deferred tool catalog by model-selected capability, category, provider, or query. Returns metadata and schema digests only.

query.description: Optional free-form model query for loaded tool names, summaries, and tags.

capability.description: Optional capability term such as search, files, memory, command, or citations.

category.description: Optional category filter. command=shell, file=filesystem; all/native/workspace mean no filter.

provider.description: Optional exact provider filter: native, mcp, or plugin. Set provider=mcp to include live MCP tools.

include_disabled.description: Whether to include disabled tools. Defaults to true.

limit.description: Maximum compact results to return, 1 through 50. Defaults to 20.

definition.name: tool_describe
definition.description: Load full invocation schemas for explicit tool catalog ids returned by tool_search. Returns schemas only for requested ids.

definition.name: tool_call
definition.description: Invoke a described progressive tool by explicit catalog id through Butler's normal guarded dispatcher.

id.description: Exact tool catalog id returned by tool_search/tool_describe.

arguments.description: Arguments matching the described target tool schema.

definition.name: list_mcp_capabilities
definition.description: List configured MCP servers and their available tools, resources, and resource templates. Use before calling an external MCP tool or reading an MCP resource.

include_disabled.description: Include disabled MCP servers in the listing.

definition.name: call_mcp_tool
definition.description: Call a tool exposed by a configured, enabled MCP server. Use list_mcp_capabilities first when the server id or tool schema is not already known.

tool_name.description: MCP tool name on that server.

arguments.description: Tool arguments matching the server-provided MCP schema.

definition.name: read_mcp_resource
definition.description: Read a resource URI exposed by a configured, enabled MCP server. Use list_mcp_capabilities first when the resource URI is not already known.

definition.name: analyze_attached_image
definition.description: Analyze one image attached to this Turn through the admitted Z.AI Vision MCP carrier. Pass the exact file_id from the current user attachment and a focused prompt; filesystem paths are not accepted.

file_id.description: Exact file_id of an image attached to the current Turn.

definition.name: create_automation
definition.description: Create a native Butler automation: a one-shot or interval scheduled prompt routed back into a Butler session.

prompt.description: Prompt to run when the automation fires.

session_id.description: Target session id. Defaults to active session.

interval_minutes.description: Interval in minutes for recurring automations.

start_at.description: Optional ISO start timestamp for interval automations.

definition.name: start_topic_conversation
definition.description: Start a new topic conversation or project from an answer in an existing Butler conversation, only when the user asks to move or split the topic. Preserves the source and carries its summarized context. Does not start execution unless follow_up is explicitly provided from the user's instruction.

title.description: Short user-facing title in the user's language.

source_session_id.description: Optional session id from conversation discovery (App, external, or canonical). Defaults to this conversation.

source_message_id.description: Optional answer id (App or canonical). Defaults to the latest completed answer in the source.

project_id.description: Existing App project id, required for destination=project.

follow_up.description: Only when the user explicitly asked to continue work there: the instruction to submit once in the new conversation. Omit to just create it.

definition.name: list_automations
definition.description: List native Butler automations with prompt previews, schedule, next run, and run counts.

definition.name: delete_automation
definition.description: Mark a native Butler automation as deleted.

definition.name: run_due_automations
definition.description: Claim due native Butler automations and return transport-neutral inbound events for gateway processing.

now.description: Optional ISO timestamp for deterministic runs.

definition.name: update_todo_list
definition.description: Create or replace Butler's durable checklist for the current non-trivial multi-step work. Reuse stable ids across updates; Butler preserves retained order and appends new ids. Keep at most one item in_progress.

list_id.description: Safe list id. Defaults to main.

todos.description: Full current todo list. The first accepted order is durable; later array reordering does not move retained ids, and new ids append.

id.description: Stable safe id. Reuse the returned id on every later update; Butler assigns one when omitted initially.

active_form.description: Present continuous form, e.g. Running validation.

phase.description: Optional Butler Turn Cognition Cycle phase for this step.

definition.name: list_todo_list
definition.description: Read Butler's durable checklist for the current work, including progress counts and the current in-progress item.

list_id.description: Safe list id. Defaults to main.

include_completed.description: When true, include completed and cancelled items.

definition.name: list_work_streams
definition.description: List Butler-owned durable WorkStreams for the active session or project. Use to preserve context switching across multiple async issues.

session_id.description: Optional session id. Defaults to the active session.

include_terminal.description: When true, include complete and failed streams.

definition.name: update_work_stream_state
definition.description: Advance or pause the active Butler-owned WorkStream through the issue-level state machine. Use for waiting_user, paused, recoverable, and explicit review/reporting transitions.

work_stream_id.description: Optional work stream id. Defaults to the active stream for this session.

active_step_id.description: Optional active step id when the state points to a known todo step.

status_note.description: Short public-safe status note. Do not include hidden reasoning or raw private text.

definition.name: control_work
definition.description: Validate or perform a transport-neutral work control action: view a result, validate resume/cancel intent, or retry failed delivery.

action.description: Control action to validate or execute.

task_id.description: Task id for view_result, resume, or cancel.

definition.name: get_memory_health
definition.description: Read Butler memory freshness, ingestion backlog, transcript count, task-memory count, and diagnostics.

definition.name: ingest_task_memory
definition.description: Ingest a completed task outcome or reviewed public report into durable task memory with provenance.

task_id.description: Completed or failed task id to ingest.

definition.name: recall_memory
definition.description: Recall source-backed associative context through graph evidence. Use evidence.read_args unchanged with read_conversation_session to inspect canonical source text.

limit.description: Maximum number of memory recall results.

include_vector.description: Whether to try vector episode search in addition to lexical, graph, project/task, and explicit memory. Defaults to true for tool calls.

time.description: Half-open ISO 8601 interval [from, to) with explicit UTC offsets.

from.description: Inclusive start, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset.

to.description: Exclusive end, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset. For a complete calendar period, use the start of the next period in the user's timezone; do not subtract a smaller time unit.

definition.name: query_memory
definition.description: Search canonical conversation scalars exactly. Phrase mode uses the literal query; any/all modes require terms and omit query. Omitting both inspects all messages allowed by the scope, time, and role filters. Use returned read_args unchanged with read_conversation_session for the complete source scalar.

query.description: Literal text for phrase mode. Omit in any/all mode. Omit both query and terms to inspect all messages allowed by the other filters.

scope.description: Canonical read scope. Explicit session/project filters only narrow this scope and never grant additional access.

project_filter.description: Use selected only with non-empty project_ids; omit project_ids for any or unassigned.

project_ids.description: Canonical project IDs that narrow selected project scope; they do not grant access.

speaker.description: Filter to user inbound messages, Butler outbound messages, or both. Defaults to any.

event_kind.description: Filter by transcript event kind. Defaults to any.

order.description: Return chronological earliest or latest matching conversation events first. Defaults to earliest.

match_mode.description: Defaults to phrase. Phrase uses query literally; any/all use the supplied terms without tokenizing query.

terms.description: Required non-empty literal terms for any/all mode. Omit in phrase mode.

case_sensitive.description: Defaults to true. False applies Unicode default case folding without changing returned text.

limit.description: Maximum number of exact conversation matches to return, 1 through 50. Defaults to 10.

time.description: Half-open ISO 8601 interval [from, to) with explicit UTC offsets.

from.description: Inclusive start, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset.

to.description: Exclusive end, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset. For a complete calendar period, use the start of the next period in the user's timezone; do not subtract a smaller time unit.

include_internal.description: Include internal recovered events when transcript recovery is explicitly requested. Defaults to false.

definition.name: summarize_user_profile
definition.description: Return Butler's reflective understanding of the principal from the consent-gated profile black box. Use when the user asks how Butler understands them. Does not expose raw profile internals.

definition.name: update_onboarding_profile
definition.description: Persist explicit answers from Butler's first-chat onboarding, including naming preferences, interests, work/main field, Butler nickname, desired treatment style, selected persona, and profile-learning consent. Use only for confirmed onboarding answers.

principal_name.description: The principal's name, if explicitly provided.

preferred_address.description: How Butler should address the principal.

butler_nickname.description: The name the principal wants Butler to use.

work.description: Explicitly shared job, profession, or main field.

service_preference.description: How the principal wants Butler to behave or treat them.

persona_preset.description: Selected persona_preset id from the first-chat onboarding context, such as operator; use custom only when the user wrote their own persona.

persona_custom.description: Custom persona/treatment text when persona_preset is custom.

profiling_mode.description: Consent-gated profile learning mode from first-chat onboarding. Set off when the principal declines or does not explicitly accept profile learning; set basic/deep only after explicit acceptance.

skipped_fields.description: Onboarding field ids the principal chose to skip.

complete.description: Set true only when onboarding is finished or the principal asks to stop onboarding.

definition.name: read_conversation_context
definition.description: Read bounded canonical conversation context for the active session. Use this to resolve references such as above, earlier, first, that one, or Korean equivalents when compact prompt context is insufficient.

anchor_message_id.description: Optional canonical conversation_message_id to read around.

anchor_event_id.description: Legacy event id to map to a canonical conversation_message_id before reading around.

direction.description: Slice direction relative to query hits or anchor event.

limit.description: Maximum number of canonical conversation messages to return.

max_chars.description: Maximum character budget for returned conversation text.

include_tools.description: Include canonical tool call/result parts when the referenced context depends on tool adjacency.

definition.name: list_conversation_sessions
definition.description: Discover canonical conversation sessions after applying scope, project, origin, and conversation-time filters. App titles are compatibility labels only.

limit.description: Maximum sessions to return, from 1 to 100.

preview_messages.description: Recent canonical user/assistant messages per session, from 1 to 6.

time.description: Half-open ISO 8601 interval [from, to) with explicit UTC offsets.

from.description: Inclusive start, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset.

to.description: Exclusive end, as an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset. For a complete calendar period, use the start of the next period in the user's timezone; do not subtract a smaller time unit.

definition.name: read_conversation_session
definition.description: Read exactly one canonical conversation session or one exact source_ref returned in recall_memory/query_memory read_args. Source mode accepts read_args unchanged and omits anchor_message_id, direction, include_tools, and limit; omit cursor on the first page and use returned cursors only with the same source.

scope.description: Read scope. Explicit session/project filters only narrow it and never grant additional access.

project_filter.description: Use selected only with non-empty project_ids; omit project_ids for any or unassigned.

project_ids.description: Canonical project IDs that narrow selected project scope; they do not grant access.

source_ref.description: Exact source locator from recall/query read_args. Use instead of conversation_session_id.

anchor_message_id.description: Optional canonical conversation_message_id to read around.

direction.description: Session-mode slice direction relative to the anchor. Defaults to before. Omit in source mode.

limit.description: Session-mode maximum canonical messages, 1 through 100. Defaults to 20. Omit in source mode.

max_chars.description: Maximum character budget. Defaults to 8,000 in session mode and 4,000 in source mode.

include_tools.description: Session mode only. Include canonical tool call/result parts when material; defaults to false. Omit in source mode.

cursor.description: Source mode only. Omit initially and pass the returned cursor unchanged for the next page.

definition.name: update_explicit_memory
definition.description: Write an explicit durable rule memory with provenance. Use only for user corrections, explicit preferences, or durable instructions.

source.description: Provenance summary, e.g. user correction message id.

definition.name: list_skills
definition.description: List Butler's machine-readable strategy skills, applicability notes, allowed tools, dispatch preference, review requirement, and validation issues.

definition.name: delegate_to_steward
definition.description: Delegate one complete Butler-authored request to an ordinary Steward session. Write the complete request exactly as the Steward should receive it; runtime preserves it unchanged instead of reconstructing it from Work or Plan state. Runtime derives delegation identity, inherited Composer access, ordinary tools, workspace, admitted context and EOL, budget, and reviewed provenance. A safe title is optional presentation metadata; omission uses a fixed privacy-safe title and never copies objective content. The Steward excludes Butler persona and direct-user presentation prompting, receives the immutable project context and bounded parent conversation projection, and returns one canonical terminal result for synthesis.

definition.name: delegate_to_worker
definition.description: Assign one bounded action from the current accepted Steward Plan to a Worker. Include a compact implementation brief with the relevant code, current state, constraints, and intended result. Steward remains responsible for integration, review, validation, and reporting.

acceptance_criteria.description: Checks for this Worker's assigned output only. Steward retains Project Ledger updates and whole-Work integration checks.

implementation_brief.description: Relevant code, current state, constraints, and the contents of applicable Spec/Plan decisions already read by Steward. References alone do not supply their contents.

definition.name: steer_steward
definition.description: Send a bounded correction or user acceptance to the original Steward and Work. Use work_id from Project Ledger for an existing open/blocked Work, including after its Steward has reported or from another conversation in the same project. Completed/abandoned Work cannot be reopened. Use relation_id for an active relation or a reported relation owned by this conversation. The original Steward owns the mutation and reports back to its original Butler conversation; queued is not completed. Never create a replacement delegation just to close existing work.

definition.name: steer_worker
definition.description: Send a bounded correction or added instruction to one active Worker relation while the Steward continues waiting for that Worker result. Continue the same Worker session and assigned work; never create a replacement Worker.

definition.name: wait_for_worker
definition.description: Suspend this Steward execution until a Worker result or direction arrives. Use after Worker assignment or steering is finished; do not execute independently while Workers are outstanding. This does not finish the Work or report to Butler. If no Worker is active, continue and handle available results.

definition.name: cancel_steward
definition.description: Stop one active Steward relation through the existing durable cancel_turn queue. Provide relation_id when more than one Steward is active.

definition.name: start_work
definition.description: Explicitly start unrelated durable Work and bind this Turn to it. Use this before dependent tools or Plan changes when the current request is new Work. Ordinary tools never select Work automatically.

objective.description: The concise stable user-visible outcome for the new Work.

definition.name: continue_work
definition.description: Explicitly bind this Turn to the exact current open Work shown in context. Use only when the current request continues that Work; ordinary tools never select it.

work_id.description: The exact candidate Work id returned in the current Work context.

definition.name: replace_work_plan
definition.description: Open or revise the Plan for the Work explicitly selected by start_work or continue_work. Revision starts planning from any current stage without a prior result review; retain completed action keys and results. Use start_new only as a compatibility translation when older callers cannot use start_work. Ordinary tools never select Work; choose start_work or continue_work before this Plan operation. Keep objective as the overall multi-Turn user outcome; put the current milestone in actions and checkpoints. Choose execution_mode during planning: Butler uses steward for substantial execution or direct for a genuinely small direct action; Steward uses direct or workers; Worker uses direct. Planning, management, integration, review, validation, and reporting stay with the current role. Do not use this for simple conversation, stable knowledge, or a single-step read-only lookup. Use it for multi-source or multi-step research with a synthesized deliverable, even when source tools are read-only.

start_new.description: True only when abandoning current open Work and starting unrelated Work.

objective.description: The concise user-visible outcome this Work must produce.

governing_refs.description: A small list of existing governing specification or document references. Use workspace-relative paths or stable document ids; do not invent references.

execution_mode.description: Who executes Plan actions: direct = this role, steward = Butler delegates to Steward, workers = Steward delegates to Workers. Preserve completed action keys when revising ownership on an existing Plan.

action_key.description: The concise stable user-visible action summary used for future progress updates, dependencies, and model continuation. Name the concrete action or outcome in the user's language, not a generic stage word.

description.description: Optional fuller detail for the action. Omit it when action_key already states the complete intended action clearly.

effect.description: Mark a high-level persistent or external change planned by this action. For contained workspace and active Project Ledger work, use plain-language capability and outcome; do not enumerate files or invent internal target strings. An exact external-effect adapter may return ordinary feedback when it needs a more specific capability or logical target.

capability.description: Plain-language change capability, or an exact tool name when the target boundary requires it.

target.description: User-meaningful outcome or exact logical target; never include a private absolute path.

definition.name: record_work_checkpoint
definition.description: Update the current Managed Work action checklist or concise progress summary when no Review is being recorded. Use it at a meaningful boundary, not to narrate every tool call. When execution starts or the current action changes, include action_updates that mark the current action active and any completed prior action done; the runtime records exactly the action keys you name. The runtime checks only known action keys and durable binding; this tool does not choose a Work stage.

public_summary.description: Optional short user-visible progress fact without secrets or private paths.

next_step.description: Optional next useful action in user-facing language.

definition.name: record_work_review
definition.description: Optionally record a concise Plan Review, result Review, or whole-Work completion Validation with the current action progress. Plan and result subjects enter review; completion enters validation against the original request, current Plan, and accepted result Review when those quality records are useful. The runtime derives the fixed graph transition from subject and verdict; never choose a raw stage. For a revised or partial result/completion, use correction_scope only to say whether correction belongs in planning or execution. When an accepted Plan enters execution, mark the first action to execute active in the same call's action_updates. The runtime validates only the fixed semantic mapping, known action keys, and durable bindings; it does not judge the Review or Validation meaning. Reviews and completion Validation are optional quality records, never completion blockers. They never change Work to completed; record_work_disposition is the sole closeout and Work-status authority. Disclosed non-critical limits may still be accepted; partial means a material requested outcome remains unfinished. A review records judgment but never replaces real tool evidence.

correction_scope.description: For a revised or partial result/completion, state where correction belongs. Omit for accepted reviews and for Plan review, whose graph edge is deterministic.

definition.name: record_work_disposition
definition.description: Atomically declare the explicitly bound Work completed, open, or blocked. This records Work state without requiring Plan, Review, or stage sequence records. Open saves progress; it does not end a delegated assignment. Steward and Worker continue actionable remaining work until completed or genuinely blocked, using the existing wait/approval flow when necessary. Completed requires every current Plan action done or skipped, no remaining actions, eligible evidence, and no unresolved or in-flight effect. Open or blocked requires a truthful remaining action or next condition; blocked also requires a concrete next condition. The Work id must be the exact id from the current bound Work context.

work_id.description: The exact Work id explicitly bound to this Turn.
